```json
{"version":"1.0.0","queries":[{"label":null,"where":{"op":"and","of":[{"op":"template_id","value":165},{"op":"time_range","since":"2005-11-29T17:33:00+00:00","until":"2005-11-29T17:43:59+00:00"}]},"limit":1000,"order":"oldest","aggregate":null}]}
```

Interpretation: the window runs from 2005-12-05T19:28 to 2005-12-06T01:28, in UTC since the corpus timestamps are UTC. Matching lines mention "uncorrectable", so I use a term match.

{"version":"1.0.0","queries":[{"label":null,"where":{"op":"and","of":[{"op":"term","value":"uncorrectable"},{"op":"time_range","since":"2005-12-05T19:28:00+00:00","until":"2005-12-06T01:28:00+00:00"}]},"limit":1000,"order":"newest","aggregate":null}]}

The schema's group_by fields are only template_id, severity and location_key. location_key is built from component:file, so grouping by it gives the breakdown by component and file in one field.


{"version":"1.0.0","queries":[{"label":"detected by location","where":{"op":"term","value":"detected"},"limit":1000,"order":"newest","aggregate":{"op":"count","group_by":["location_key"],"having":null}}]}

The aggregate can only group by template_id, severity or location_key, and "component" maps to location_key (component:file). "Message type" maps to template_id. So I group by location_key and template_id, and bound the time range to 09:45–15:45 UTC on 2005-12-09.

{"version":"1.0.0","queries":[{"label":"count by component and template","where":{"op":"time_range","since":"2005-12-09T09:45:00+00:00","until":"2005-12-09T15:45:00+00:00"},"limit":1000,"order":"newest","aggregate":{"op":"count","group_by":["location_key","template_id"],"having":null}}]}

The question asks for counts per logger (component), so I need an aggregate over a time window. The available group_by fields are template_id, severity and location_key, and location_key is built from component and file, so I group by it. The "at least 50" condition becomes a `min_count` of 50 in `having`.

```json
{"version":"1.0.0","queries":[{"label":"loggers with at least 50 messages","where":{"op":"time_range","since":"2017-05-17T08:42:54+00:00","until":"2017-05-17T09:42:54+00:00"},"limit":1000,"order":"newest","aggregate":{"op":"count","group_by":["location_key"],"having":{"min_count":50,"max_count":null}}}]}
```

Interpretation: "each log message" means each message type, so the grouping is by template_id and location_key (component:file). The "at least 10 times" threshold is applied per group, so the count has min_count 10. The window is 06:05:43 to 07:05:43 UTC on 2017-05-17.

```json
{"version":"1.0.0","queries":[{"label":null,"where":{"op":"time_range","since":"2017-05-17T06:05:43+00:00","until":"2017-05-17T07:05:43+00:00"},"limit":1000,"order":"newest","aggregate":{"op":"count","group_by":["template_id","location_key"],"having":{"min_count":10,"max_count":null}}}]}
```

The question asks for counts per message (template_id) and per component and log file (location_key). That is two group_by fields at most, so I can't group by all three. The question says "each distinct log message show up per component and log file", which makes three dimensions. I'll keep template_id and location_key, since location_key already combines component and file.

The time window runs from 05:29 on May 17 to 05:29 on May 18, 2017 UTC. The having filter is min_count 2.

The question asks for lines from either of two sources. "nova-api WSGI server" is most likely nova.osapi_compute.wsgi.server in nova-api.log. nova.metadata.wsgi.server is also a WSGI server, but the metadata server is a different service from the nova-api one, so I'll use osapi only. The resource claims logger is nova.compute.claims in nova-compute.log. I'll combine these with an OR of two location_key terms and use limit 1000.

